answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by requiring each identity to stake a meaningful, refundable deposit before it can transact — the way a meadow's gatekeeper charges admission only once per traveler. Cheap clones can't multiply, because each new identity pays the same stake, and a knoll of honest peers can slash the deposit when an agent misbehaves. Ivory-tower theory aside, the math works: forging a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes, so attackers pay more than any fraud could earn.
